recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not re-add the CapabilityStatement.implementation.custodian trial-use marker unless a new R6+ governance decision explicitly reinstates element-level STU markers inside normative core resources.
issue_request: FHIR-16342 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I change request for STU3 that accepted adding CapabilityStatement.implementation.custodian as Reference(Organization) 0..1 with organization-management/oversight semantics and an R4 STU flag.
initial_application: Historical git commit 5b7c6d6d2e added CapabilityStatement.implementation.custodian to the then-authoritative spreadsheet with Reference(Organization), 0..1, summary=true, the requested definition, and trial-use status. The 2021 source rework commit 33b409a4b6 preserved the element and trial-use marker in structuredefinition-CapabilityStatement.xml.
additional_context: CapabilityStatement is active in source/fhir.ini and current structuredefinition-CapabilityStatement.xml still contains custodian with the requested cardinality, type, target profile, short description, and definition. Published R4/R5 JSON had the trial-use marker, but current build JSON lacks it because commit 5c20769cc7 removed CapabilityStatement element-level trial-use markers during later R6 status cleanup. The already-published FHIR-40493 reconciliation on the combined branch documents why those R5-era markers should not be reintroduced without a new FMG/FHIR-I decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The substantive custodian element is present, and restoring only the old STU marker for this seed would conflict with later normative-status history.

related_jiras.note: Existing combined-branch audit explains that R5 trial-use markers on normative artifacts were applied historically but intentionally left absent after R6 normative-status cleanup.
No-change decision discusses value set/code system status for TU elements in normative resources and confirms the surrounding status-policy context without requiring a custodian source edit.
